title: Asynchronous Role Transition and Shadowing Protocol
author: Hannah Li
body:
Summary

This playbook defines Redwood Inference’s Asynchronous Role Transition and Shadowing Protocol (ARTS). ARTS is designed for distributed teams and international hires to enable predictable, low-friction role handoffs, manager-to-manager transitions, and individual contributor (IC) role changes without requiring full-time synchronous overlap. It complements existing onboarding and 90-day playbooks by providing concrete checklists, timelines, and templates for staggered knowledge transfer, risk mitigation, and role certification.

Scope

- Applies to: voluntary internal role changes, manager handoffs, position backfills, and long-lead external hires where synchronous overlap is limited (timezones, parental leave, extended notice).
- Excludes: emergency replacements for critical oncall-only roles (see Oncall Runbook).
- Cross-functional: recommended for eng, product, customer-success, and platform teams, but adaptable to sales and go-to-market.

Objectives

1. Maintain service continuity and SLO adherence during transitions.
2. Minimize cognitive load on incumbents while preserving knowledge quality.
3. Provide a clear, auditable path to role readiness and certification.
4. Enable distributed contributors and international hires to onboard and ramp at variable paces.

Roles & Ownership

- Outgoing Owner (OO): current role holder; responsible for creating knowledge artifacts and shadowing plan.
- Incoming Owner (IO): person taking the role; responsible for completing checklists and asking clarifying questions.
- Transition Lead (TL): usually the hiring manager or people-ops partner; coordinates timeline and approves certification.
- Team Steward: a senior IC or manager who verifies operational runbooks, schedules handoff checkpoints, and owns risk mitigations.
- People Ops Partner: monitors compliance with company transition SLAs and facilitates tools (access requests, training credits).

Transition Categories and SLAs

1. Short Transition (notice <= 2 weeks): SLA = 3 business days to complete ARTS artifacts and schedule 2 synchronous checkpoints.
2. Standard Transition (2-8 weeks): SLA = document + 4 asynchronous shadow epochs + 1 final 1:1 live walkthrough.
3. Staggered / Long Transition (>8 weeks or geographic constraints): SLA = staged handoff with weekly digest updates and formal role certification meeting within first 30 days of start.

High-level Steps (timelines vary by category)

1. Kickoff (Day 0–2 after role acceptance/notice)
   - TL creates a Transition Page in Confluence using the ARTS template.
   - People Ops opens an access ticket (Okta/GCP/AWS) flagged "transition" with target dates.
   - OO attaches 3 priority artifacts: (a) Runbook summary, (b) Current roadmap and outstanding tickets, (c) Known risks and mitigation steps.

2. Artifact Authoring (Days 1–7 for Short; 1–21 for Standard)
   - OO writes a 5-minute orientation doc: purpose, 3 key metrics owner tracks, daily cadence.
   - OO creates a 1-page "Decision Map": what decisions the role is empowered to make and delegation thresholds.
   - OO annotates 3 canonical playbooks (runbooks, postmortems, escalation flows) with inline links to code and dashboards.

3. Asynchronous Shadowing Epochs (Standard and Staggered flows)
   - An epoch is a 48–72 hour observation window where IO consumes artifacts and posts clarifying questions via Confluence comments or Slack thread.
   - Recommended cadence: 4 epochs spaced across the transition window. Each epoch ends with the IO publishing a short "learning log" (3 bullet takeaways + 2 open risks).

4. Validation & Role Certification (Final week)
   - Team Steward performs operational checks using the Role Readiness Checklist (table below).
   - TL schedules a 60-minute certification meeting; IO demonstrates: ticket triage, a simulated incident run, and an example prioritization decision.
   - People Ops updates HR record and flags the role completion in the onboarding dashboard.

Role Readiness Checklist (use as table on the Transition Page)

| Area | Minimum Artifact / Evidence | Owner | Status |
|-----|----------------------------|-------|--------|
| Access & Tools | Verified access to repo(s), dashboards, pager, CI | People Ops / TL | TODO |
| Runbooks | 1-page summary + 1 runbook annotated in last 6 months | OO | TODO |
| Incidents | Participation in 1 incident post-transition with debrief | IO | TODO |
| Codebase | Successful PR and code review in area | IO | TODO |
| Product Context | One roadmap walkthrough with PM and 3 prioritized goals | TL/PM | TODO |
| Stakeholders | Intro notes sent to 5 primary partners | IO | TODO |

Minimum Deliverables (templates provided at bottom)

- Transition Page (Confluence): purpose, timeline, checkpoints, links.
- 5-minute orientation doc (text + 2 minute screencast recommended).
- Decision Map (markdown table).
- 4 learning logs (if Standard flow).
- Final certification recording (optional).

Communication Patterns and Channels

- Primary async channel: dedicated Slack thread named #transitions-<role>-<month>. Use pinned message to surface the Transition Page.
- Confluence is the single source of truth. Do not duplicate artifacts across Google Drive for ARTS items.
- For cross-timezone legal/HR steps (visa, background checks), People Ops will add a separate checklist to the Transition Page and tag the IO.

Risk Mitigations and Fallbacks

- If OO becomes unavailable during transition: TL appoints an Interim Steward within 48 hours and adds an "Interim Notes" section to the Transition Page.
- If IO shows gaps during certification: TL may extend shadow epochs up to 30 days; for critical roles, TL requests a temporary buddy assignment.

Manager Guidance (for hiring/receiving managers)

- Plan transitions as projects. Allocate 4 hours/week for the first 2 weeks to actively coach IO.
- Prefer small, measurable milestones: first PR merged, first triage rotation, first stakeholder update.
- Use the "2-week triage" metric: IO should be able to independently triage 3 incoming tickets in the first 14 days.

People Ops Responsibilities

- Provision access as priority tickets with "transition" tag and 72-hour SLA.
- Maintain ARTS template and ensure TLs create Transition Pages for every internal move.
- Track and report two metrics monthly: average time-to-certification and percentage of transitions requiring >30 day remediation.

Metrics & Success Criteria

- Target: 75% of Standard transitions certified within 21 days of start.
- Target: <10% of transitions trigger >30-day remediation.
- Operational signal: mean time between incidents in the first 60 days should not regress more than 10% vs pre-transition baseline.

Templates (copyable snippets)

1) Confluence Transition Page header (paste into new page):

Title: [Role] Transition - [Incoming Name] - [Month YYYY]
Transition Lead: [Name]
Start Date: [YYYY-MM-DD]
Certification Target Date: [YYYY-MM-DD]
Status: draft / in_progress / certified

2) 5-minute orientation doc template:
- Purpose: one sentence
- Scope & boundaries: what this role does NOT own (3 bullets)
- 3 metrics I watch daily/weekly
- Weekly cadence & recurring meetings
- Where to find runbooks and dashboards (links)

3) Sample Slack opener (send by IO, after epoch 1):
Hi team — I’m [Incoming Name], onboarding into [role]. I’ve completed epoch 1 and my top open questions are: 1) [short], 2) [short]. Happy to take any pointers or suggest pairing sessions.

FAQs

Q: When is synchronous overlap mandatory?
A: Mandatory for any role that is primary oncall for customer-facing services (minimum 3 days overlap). See Oncall Runbook.

Q: Who signs off on access changes?
A: TL + People Ops must both sign the access ticket before IO assumes production privileges.

Q: Can ARTS be used for part-time contractors?
A: Yes. For contractors, TL should reduce artifact requirements proportionally and ensure billing/contract alignment with Finance.

Appendix: Automation ideas (future roadmap)

- Auto-create Transition Page from an HR event when someone accepts an internal role in Workday.
- Slack bot to nudge IOs to post learning logs at epoch boundaries.
- Dashboard widget in Redwood Console for "Transitions in Progress" with pass/fail certification signals.
